# Bootstrap 5.3.9 runtime theme control map

This is a map of runtime controls and possible override targets, not an implementation or final set of theme-token names. It complements the [Sass derivation audit](theme-variable-audit.md). The distribution remains unchanged.

## How to use this map

1. Start with the [relationship map](#1-related-reference-values-and-runtime-control). Values are grouped by their audited Sass reference and expression; follow a pattern link to the original derivation and source. Each row says **where** the Bootstrap custom property is assigned.
2. Use the [fixed and mixed declaration inventory](#2-ordinary-visual-declarations) to find visual properties Bootstrap sets outside `--bs-*` variables. A non-variable declaration is an **override candidate**, not necessarily something that should change: `inherit`, `currentColor`, `0`, browser-specific rules and structural resets can be intentional.
3. Convert the desired decisions into framework-independent core, computed and optional component tokens later. A single token may feed many rows, but identical defaults alone are not evidence of a shared design decision.

**CSS source and scope:** `src/bootstrap/reference/css/bootstrap.css`, Bootstrap 5.3.9. The source link in each row points to its line. The inventory includes separate selectors, media/supports contexts, states and `!important` declarations. The bundled LTR CSS is the baseline; test the shipped RTL, reboot, grid and utilities variants separately before claiming identical coverage. The Sass source map is from an expanded compilation of official tag `v5.3.9` (`349bdb50b8ab6782248c1b296443087cd7222ead`); mapped Sass locations are navigation hints, not proof of the complete derivation. No Sass source or build dependency is added to the repository.

**Scope of ordinary CSS:** colour/background, border/outline/radius, typography/text, spacing, sizing, shadow/opacity/filter, motion/transform, generated content and list decoration. It includes shorthands and longhands, including constants, mixed `var()` expressions and utility classes. It does **not** claim all layout/behaviour declarations, every possible CSS property, selector interactions, user-agent styling, JavaScript-generated states, all asset colours, or breakpoint parameters have been resolved. `@media` thresholds are not runtime custom properties. Some properties such as `content`, `width` and animation may be structural rather than theme decisions. Source-map mismatches are marked `—`; inspect those rules directly. Verify use and specificity in a browser before implementing.

**Coverage:** 1186 Bootstrap custom-property declaration contexts (449 unique names); 2957 ordinary visual declarations (2141 with no `var()`, 816 with `var()`), including 2935 Sass-mapped ordinary declarations. A context is one declaration in one selector and enclosing at-rule, not a count of individual elements affected. The inventory is intentionally broader than a list of mandatory overrides.

## Runtime control: what actually needs an override

| Situation | What must be set | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Root default is a literal | Set the root property, and separately set any compiled derived property or RGB companion that should track it. | `--bs-primary` and `--bs-primary-rgb` are separate outputs ([CSS 32–40](../../src/bootstrap/reference/css/bootstrap.css#L32)). |
| Component assigns a literal `--bs-*` | Assign that same component-scoped property on the relevant selector; setting an identically named property only on an ancestor loses to the component's own declaration. | `.btn-primary` sets `--bs-btn-bg`, hover, active, focus and disabled values ([CSS 3034](../../src/bootstrap/reference/css/bootstrap.css#L3034)). |
| Component assigns `var(--bs-…)` | Control the referenced property where the alias is computed, unless a more specific rule overrides it. | `.alert-primary` uses the primary emphasis/subtle aliases ([CSS 4875](../../src/bootstrap/reference/css/bootstrap.css#L4875)). |
| Ordinary property contains a literal and no variable | Add a CSS rule for the selector/state if the theme should change that decision. | `.form-check-input[type=checkbox]` sets `border-radius: 0.25em` ([CSS 2413](../../src/bootstrap/reference/css/bootstrap.css#L2413)). |
| Ordinary property mixes variables and constants | Set the referenced variables for the portions they control; override the declaration if its fixed portions must change. | `.form-control` uses `border: var(--bs-border-width) solid var(--bs-border-color)`; `solid` is fixed ([CSS 2132](../../src/bootstrap/reference/css/bootstrap.css#L2132)). |
| Utility or state rule wins in the cascade | Match/beat specificity, cascade order and, where needed, `!important`; preserve responsive and pseudo-element contexts. | `.text-primary` reads `--bs-primary-rgb` with `!important` ([CSS 8511](../../src/bootstrap/reference/css/bootstrap.css#L8511)); `.pb-1` is a fixed `!important` ([CSS 8257](../../src/bootstrap/reference/css/bootstrap.css#L8257)). |

Custom properties are computed on the element where they are declared and inherited as computed values. In particular, changing an input on a **descendant** does not necessarily recompute an alias inherited from an ancestor. Dark-mode selectors and nested themes can redeclare inputs; set aliases at the appropriate scope and test the actual cascade. Inline styles, third-party CSS and Shadow DOM can also change the result. A runtime `var()` dependency is not the same thing as a compile-time Sass dependency.

## Worked relationships: primary, surfaces and scales

For the six chromatic theme colours (primary, secondary, success, info, warning and danger), Bootstrap defines separate light and dark semantic roles; light and dark theme colours have special definitions, so do not generalise the same formulas to them. Bootstrap's `tint-color(c, w)` mixes white into `c` by weight `w`; `shade-color(c, w)` mixes black into it. These are Sass mixes, not generic HSL-lightness adjustments.

| Relationship / default derivation | Bootstrap targets and runtime action |
|---|---|
| Direct primary | Root `--bs-primary` is `#0d6efd`, but `.btn-primary` and checked form controls also contain separate compiled literals. Set the root, component variables, and fixed checkbox/radio declarations as applicable. |
| 60% shade of primary in light mode | `--bs-primary-text-emphasis: #052c65`; alerts/list-group aliases can follow this value, but it does not recalculate when `--bs-primary` changes. |
| 80% tint / 60% tint in light mode | `--bs-primary-bg-subtle: #cfe2ff` and `--bs-primary-border-subtle: #9ec5fe` respectively. Keep the two calculations separate; assign both outputs. |
| 40% tint, 80% shade, 40% shade in dark mode | Dark `--bs-primary-text-emphasis: #6ea8fe`, `--bs-primary-bg-subtle: #031633`, `--bs-primary-border-subtle: #084298`; update the dark selector separately. |
| Primary button state calculations | `.btn-primary` hover background `shade-color($primary, 15%)`; hover border and active background use `shade-color($primary, 20%)`; active border uses `shade-color($primary, 25%)`. Each is a component custom-property assignment, not a root alias. Foreground and focus RGB also require separate contrast/mix calculations. Other variants choose tint/shade according to their Sass branch; verify each variant rather than assuming primary's rule. |
| Focus border | `.form-control:focus`, `.form-select:focus`, and `.form-check-input:focus` use the fixed `#86b7fe`, from `tint-color($component-active-bg, 50%)` with `$component-active-bg: $primary` by default (`scss/_variables.scss:566,915`). Their fixed focus shadow also needs control. These are ordinary CSS declarations, not component custom-property assignments. |
| RGB, contrast and opacity | `--bs-primary-rgb` is a separate comma-separated RGB value; utilities consume it along with opacity. `color-contrast(...)`, `mix(...)`, `rgba(...)` and RGB conversion are different operations and must not be merged merely because their outputs match. |
| Radius scale | Several component variables reference `--bs-border-radius*`, but others have scoped literals or fixed property declarations. `border-radius: 0` is frequently a structural reset, not necessarily a design token. Set the scale, then address only relevant component contexts and fixed rules. |
| Spacing | `.btn` exposes padding custom properties, `.form-control` uses fixed `padding: 0.375rem 0.75rem`, and `.pb-*` utilities hardcode the spacing scale with `!important`. Form-control padding traces through `$input-padding-y/x` to `$input-btn-padding-y/x`, also used by the button variables; the spacing utilities come from `$spacers`. Similar defaults do not prove these separate Sass definitions share a reference. A root spacer alone does not recalculate those rules. |
| Body, text and borders | Body/background, emphasis, secondary/tertiary surfaces and border roots have colour and RGB companions; many components consume aliases but others declare their own literals. Treat semantic roles and their dark variants separately. |

**Audit correction:** the previous audit's summary says dark link colours are independent `$blue-300`/`$blue-200`. The official v5.3.9 defaults instead define `$link-color-dark: tint-color($primary, 40%)` and `$link-hover-color-dark: shift-color($link-color-dark, -$link-shade-percentage)` (`scss/_variables-dark.scss:53–54`). They still compile to fixed CSS outputs and do not update automatically at runtime. The audit's more detailed primary-pattern rows show the latter relationship. Also, a raw `--bs-primary` change alone does **not** update alerts: their aliases follow `--bs-primary-text-emphasis` / `-bg-subtle` / `-border-subtle` only when those derived properties are updated.

**Other important unresolved cases:** embedded SVG data URLs bake in icon colours; to recolour them requires an appropriate component property or replacement image/rule, not just changing a root colour. Contrast choice must be validated for actual foreground/background pairs and states. Colour mixing support, colour spaces, alpha compositing, dynamic contrast, browser support and fallback strategy remain design decisions. Dark-mode targets can differ from light targets. Do not equate palette steps, light/dark variants, fixed constants, or mixed expressions based only on equal compiled values.

## 1. Related reference values and runtime control

The following groups reuse the previous audit's reference anchors and expression patterns. **They are a research index, not verified equivalence classes:** the audit uses heuristic anchoring, and its Sass expression expansion can be incomplete or incorrect. A pattern link shows the original tracing; check the official Sass when exact derivation matters, especially dark aliases, maps, mixin arguments and embedded SVGs. A value equal to another default does not establish a dependency. Original subgroup headings may abbreviate long expressions; follow the link for the full version.

**Action key:** `root literal` = set at the appropriate root/theme scope; `scoped literal` = override on the listed selector; `alias` = set its input at the scope where the alias is computed or override the alias itself. This identifies the declaration, not whether a component actually consumes it. A root selector can also be emitted later by a component, so check cascade order. `—` means no enclosing at-rule.

## 1b. Fixed declarations sharing directly traced Sass references

The following is a conservative **subset**, not a complete trace of the fixed CSS inventory. It groups ordinary no-`var()` declarations whose mapped Sass source is a direct `$variable` assignment, following only unambiguous, simple default-variable aliases. Values sharing a terminal name share that Sass reference; different terminal names are not grouped merely because their defaults match. Inspect the Sass source for conditional overrides and build-time context before treating these as a single runtime token. Calculations, maps, mixin parameters, RFS and unmatched/autoprefixed output require further work and remain in section 2.

143 declaration contexts in 80 terminal-reference groups.

## 2. Ordinary visual declarations

Every row below is an ordinary CSS declaration in the defined property-family scope. **No `var()`** identifies a candidate for a selector-level override if its value must change; constants can still be inherited or relative, so this is not proof of an independent value. **Contains `var()`** lists dependencies and fixed portions together; do not assume setting one input controls the complete declaration. `!important` is shown explicitly. A Sass source-map link identifies a likely generating line; generated utility/mixin arguments and intermediate variables require further tracing. `—` means the shipped declaration could not be matched exactly to the temporary compilation (often autoprefixer differences), not that no Sass source exists.

| Colour and surfaces | 109 | 253 |
| Generated content and decoration | 25 | 1 |
| Motion and transforms | 114 | 13 |
| Shadows, opacity and filters | 42 | 30 |
| Sizing | 288 | 62 |
| Spacing | 1097 | 106 |
| Typography and text | 250 | 59 |

## 3. Remaining work before implementation

- Trace each ordinary CSS override candidate to its actual Sass variable, map/mixin argument or independent constant. The source-map hints narrow the search; this document does not claim that all fixed values have been assigned to verified reference/derivation groups.
- Resolve component-local aliases and cascade interactions in actual markup, including nested light/dark themes, component variants, states, utilities and RTL.
- Decide which candidates are intentional structural resets or browser compatibility rules, and which represent configurable visual decisions. Keep values separate until the source or a deliberate design decision establishes a relationship.
- Create the master token register and mapping, including output format for RGB companions, contrast choices, image assets, responsive behaviour, configuration/override precedence, and browser support; then test representative themes and accessibility.
